plain_language.comparison_summary: Compared before (n=21, mean=0.06509) against after (n=24, mean=0.02551) using Welch's two-sample t-test (unequal variances assumed by default -- no equal-variance check to trip on).
plain_language.effect_size_in_words: Cohen's d = 1.75 -- a large difference (Cohen 1988 conventional bands: negligible<0.2, small<0.5, medium<0.8, large>=0.8).
plain_language.p_value_meaning: p = 0.0000, below the alpha=0.05 threshold: if there were truly no difference, a result at least this far from 'no difference' would turn up by chance alone only about 0.00024% of the time. That makes the difference statistically detectable here -- it does not mean the null hypothesis is false with that probability, and it says nothing yet about whether the difference is big enough to matter.
plain_language.practical_significance_prompt: Statistically detectable ≠ big enough to matter -- compare the effect size above against the goal.
